# Best Reverse Osmosis Systems

> Independent, research-based comparisons of under-sink reverse osmosis systems, countertop purifiers and replacement filters for US kitchens. We compare published specifications, third-party certifications, live pricing and the yearly cost of the cartridges. We do not physically test products, we do not run a testing lab, and we never invent ratings — Amazon no longer exposes verified rating data through its product API, so you will find no star scores anywhere on this site.

## Top picks (2026)

- **Best overall — Waterdrop G3P600 (~$439):** tankless, 600 GPD, 2:1 drain ratio, 8 stages. Certified to NSF/ANSI 58 for TDS reduction *and* NSF/ANSI 372 for lead-free materials. Smart faucet showing live TDS and filter life; cartridges change with one twist. Needs an outlet.
- **Best value tankless — Waterdrop G2P600 (~$299):** same 600 GPD tankless form factor and 2:1 drain ratio, 7 stages, 30-minute install. Carries NSF/ANSI 372 (materials) only, not the 58 performance certification.
- **Cheapest to run — iSpring RCC7AK-BN (~$199):** classic tank system, 75 GPD, 6 stages with an alkaline remineralization stage, certified as a whole system to NSF/ANSI 58. Universal 10" x 2.5" cartridges make a full year of replacements about $69.
- **Best built — APEC Water ROES-PH75 (~$240):** WQA-certified 75 GPD tank system with calcium remineralization, heavy standard-size housings, and a $25.46 pre-filter set changed twice a year.
- **Best without an outlet — Frizzlife M800 (~$300):** non-electric tankless running on line pressure, up to 900 GPD, certified to NSF/ANSI 58 & 372, and the best efficiency here at a claimed 4:1 pure-to-drain. Tall: 14.5 x 5.1 x 19.7 inches.
- **Best for renters — Bluevua RO100ROPOT-Lite (~$219):** countertop, plug-and-play, 7 stages with UV and a glass carafe. No plumbing, no drilling; sized for one or two people.

## How to choose

- **Cabinet space:** a tank system is three housings plus a pressure tank; a tankless unit is one slim box. Measure height and the depth behind the P-trap first.
- **Certification:** NSF/ANSI 58 certifies contaminant and TDS reduction. NSF/ANSI 372 only certifies lead-free materials. WQA is a separate certifying body. They are not interchangeable.
- **Drain ratio:** RO sends some water to the drain. Older systems run 3:1 or 4:1 against you; modern tankless units are commonly 2:1, and the Frizzlife M800 claims 4:1 in your favour.
- **Filter economics:** systems using universal 10" x 2.5" cartridges cost roughly $25-$70 a year; proprietary twist-in cartridges cost more but change in seconds.
- **Power:** most tankless systems need a GFCI outlet under the sink. Tank systems and the Frizzlife M800 do not.

## Method

We pulled every reverse osmosis system, under-sink filter and replacement cartridge we could source from Amazon's catalogue — 85 products — and kept those with a complete published specification: rated output, drain ratio, stage count, cartridge part numbers and a named certification. We compare specifications, certifications and the price of every replacement cartridge, and read the critical owner reviews closely. We do not physically test these systems.
